subject: toucan
pitch: A keel-billed toucan showing off on a short mossy branch. A huge rainbow beak in lime green, sky blue and orange with a cherry-red tip, a glossy black body, a lemon-yellow bib, a ring of lime-green skin around each eye, bright blue feet and a scarlet patch under the tail. A single pink orchid blooms on the branch beside it.
reasoning:
I'm sketching proportions for a stylized toucan - scaling up the beak size relative to a real toucan, and planning how it perches on a horizontal branch positioned just above the ground plane.

Now I'm designing the skeleton hierarchy: root at body center, with spine, neck, head, and jaw joints for the bill, plus leg chains to the branch and a tail and folded wing joints. I'm also working out the body's position and tilt, rotating a scaled sphere so its long axis angles from an upright chest down to a trailing tail.

Now I'm shaping the beak as a tapered sweep extending from the head, and planning a toucan-style color gradient along its length—lime near the base transitioning through orange and blue bands toward the tip, using position-based paint logic to assign colors by z-coordinate and surface normal.

Now I'm setting up the lower beak as a smaller sweep attached to the jaw bone, positioning it to overlap slightly with the upper beak for a closed mouth, and planning the head as a black sphere.

Adding the yellow bib patch at the throat and chest with a slightly overlapping ellipsoid, placing the head and a softer yellow neck sphere underneath, then flattening a lime-green ring shape for the eye socket on each side of the head.

Now I'm working out the eye position: a dark brown iris sphere with a black pupil and tiny highlight, placed just outside the skin ring, and checking the math so the eye sits properly on the head's curved surface without poking through.

For the skeleton, I'm setting up the neck and head joints with approximate positions and planning to chain them manually with named roles for the rigging.

Then I'm sketching the tail as a swept chain from a curved catmull-rom path starting near the hips.

For the tail geometry, I'll give it a flat, tapering cross-section and a dark black color, then add a small scarlet patch under the tail base to mimic an undertail covert marking. Now I'm moving on to the wings, planning to keep them folded flat along the body sides.

Each wing I'll build as a sweep chain running from the shoulder joint down to the tip, deciding whether to use a flattened tube cross-section or instead extrude a side-profile outline to get the right thin, flattened wing shape.

Finishing the wing outline back to the starting point, confirming it's a simple non-crossing polygon, then setting bevel and smoothing values. I'm checking that the wing's position relative to the body ellipsoid keeps it floating just outside the surface given the body's width tapering at front and back.

For the body I'll keep it a simple black sphere and skip the white rump detail for now. For the legs, I'm placing hip, knee, and ankle joints tucked under the body with thin blue capsule segments, then adding zygodactyl toes (two forward, two back) resting flat on the branch.

Adding toe geometry and claws...

I need a dedicated root joint at the origin with hips as a child, and a separate branch joint since a prop can't share the bird's root. For the branch itself, mottled brown-green coloring and moss clumps made of flattened spheres with tiny twigs and leaves scattered randomly along its length should give it a natural look.

Positioning the moss away from where the bird's feet grip the branch, I'll also add rounded caps on the cut ends and a small orchid growing beside the bird with a thin arching stem and a pink phalaenopsis-style bloom made of five petals.

Building petal geometry...

I'm adding two more leaf ellipsoids at the branch base, then thinking through how scale and rotation compose for the flower parts and making sure every part gets an explicit bone assignment, defaulting to root for the orchid and using a helper function to keep it consistent. I'm also noting bird details like a white throat patch for the toucan still need defining.

Now I'm working out the toucan's head markings—a dark ring at the beak base, a tiny nostril sphere positioned along the beak's curve, and figuring out how the beak's radius tapers along its length to place these features accurately.

Still defining beak geometry...

Still defining beak colors...

Adding more body geometry...

Working through the transform, I find the body surface already extends past z~.13 at that height, so the bib sphere pokes out front and covers the chest nicely. That confirms the eye rings and cheek placement are fine, so I'm moving on to sizing the head sphere with its scale factors.

Now I'm setting up a shared sphere geometry to reuse across body parts for efficiency, then defining the tail as a three-link chain following a smooth curve path from the hips, tapering its radius toward the tip.

Setting up the tail taper formula with rounded caps, then moving to leg structure: wing joints tagged with roles, thigh capsules in blue, and hip/knee joint positions for a hidden-knee bird leg rig.

Defining toe joints and capsules branching from the ankle...

I'll adjust the branch radius slightly so it sinks a bit for the feet to rest on, then add small black claw spikes at each toe tip, and sprinkle in moss clumps using scaled green spheres in varying shades for texture.

Placing the orchid stem rising from the branch at x=0.2, curving up to a flower centered around (0.225, 0.2), facing forward toward the viewer alongside the bird. I'm checking proportions so the petals, spanning roughly 0.13 wide, stay clear of the bird's wing and beak.

Placing the leaves now, two flattened elongated ellipsoids near the stem base, angled outward with slight tilts so they read as orchid foliage framing the stem.

I'm layering the flower parts front to back—sepals, petals, lip, column—and adding small magenta accent spheres near the petal centers. I'm also considering the toucan's layered details, like a thin red-orange band beneath the chest bib to match the real bird's coloring.

I decide to skip the white rump patch and tail detailing for simplicity, keeping things focused on the beak's base ring in black paint rather than adding serrations or ridge highlights. Now I'm setting up the geometry helpers, starting with a reusable sphere geometry and a placement function for positioning, scaling, rotating, and naming each body part.

Writing joint hierarchy setup...

Now I'm setting up the tail as a chain of bones using a smooth curve, then sweeping geometry along it with rounded caps. I'm also adding a branch sweep with a slightly tapered radius using a sine-based variation, keeping it anchored to the root bone.

For the branch coloring, I'm blending a mottled bark texture with a mossy green tint that gets stronger toward the top surface, using a smoothstep based on surface normal.

Now moving into the wing extrusion setup, defining position, orientation, and thickness parameters...

Adding a blue sheen gradient for the body paint, then setting up the toucan builder with jaw and head joints, eye details with pupil and catchlight, and the under-beak sweep matching the main beak coloring.
